requirements.description: Export createServer() from src/index.ts. It returns an unstarted Node HTTP server, and notes are stored in memory per server instance.
When src/index.ts is executed directly, the server listens on PORT, defaulting to 3000 when PORT is not provided.

POST /notes accepts a JSON body with a text field. The text must be a string whose trimmed value is nonempty. On success, store the trimmed text and return status 201 with a JSON object containing a string id and the stored text. Malformed JSON and missing, empty, whitespace-only, or non-string text return status 400.
GET /notes returns status 200 and a JSON array of all notes for that server instance in insertion order.
GET /notes/:id returns the matching note, or status 404 when no note with that id exists.
DELETE /notes/:id returns status 204 for an existing note, or status 404 for an unknown id.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Calling createServer() returns an unstarted Node HTTP server that does not serve requests until listen is called. Two server instances created in the same process have separate note stores: a note posted to the first server is returned by the first server's GET /notes and is absent from the second server's GET /notes.
When the entry point is executed directly with PORT unset, the server listens on port 3000. When executed directly with PORT set to an available port, the server listens on that port.

POST /notes with JSON body {"text":"  alpha  "} returns status 201 and a JSON object whose id is a string and whose text is exactly "alpha". A following GET /notes returns an array containing that note with text exactly "alpha", verifying trimming on a noncanonical valid input and exact normalized storage/return.
POST /notes with malformed JSON returns status 400.
POST /notes returns status 400 when text is missing, an empty string, a whitespace-only string, or a non-string JSON value.

GET /notes on a new server returns status 200 and an empty JSON array. After posts for notes A then B, GET /notes returns status 200 and a JSON array containing A then B in insertion order with the stored normalized text.
After creating a note, GET /notes/:id returns the matching note. GET /notes/:id for an unknown id returns status 404.
DELETE /notes/:id for an existing note returns status 204, and a subsequent GET /notes/:id returns status 404. DELETE /notes/:id for an unknown id returns status 404.
Requests to unknown routes, such as GET /unknown or POST /unknown, return status 404.

constraints: Use TypeScript and Node.js built-in modules only.
Export createServer() from src/index.ts and return an unstarted Node HTTP server.
Store notes in memory per server instance; do not share note storage between server instances.
For POST /notes, normalize text by trimming before storage and return; validation checks the trimmed value is nonempty.
Do not add authentication, a database, a frontend, or external service dependencies.
Tests should use port 0 and close their servers.
ambiguities: The exact id generation format and id uniqueness mechanism are not specified; only that id is a string and identifies a note for GET/DELETE paths.
The response body and Content-Type for 400 and 404 errors are not specified.
Behavior for unsupported HTTP methods on known paths, such as PUT /notes/:id, is not specified; only unknown routes are required to return 404.
Trailing-slash handling and URL-decoding behavior for /notes/:id are not specified.
Whether POST /notes accepts or rejects extra JSON properties beyond text is not specified.
Direct-execution behavior for startup errors such as port-in-use is not specified.
outOfScope: Updating or editing notes; no PUT or PATCH behavior is specified.
Pagination, filtering, or sorting beyond insertion-order retrieval.
